title: Replication package: Normalisation as implicit re-weighting in multi-criteria portfolio selection: closed form and cost against an exact Pareto frontier

creators.name: Azancort Neto, Julio Leite
creators.affiliation: Instituto de Tecnologia, Universidade Federal do Para (UFPA), Belem, PA, Brazil

description:
Replication package for Normalisation as implicit re-weighting in multi-criteria portfolio selection: closed form and cost against an exact Pareto frontier (under review at Omega, Elsevier).

Contents (v1.2): (i) input data for 473 candidate landfill sites on Fogo Island, Cabo Verde; (ii) pre-registration documents for six sub-experiments and the main factorial (PRESPEC_E1–E6, PRESPEC_R1, PRESPEC_SANTIAGO); (iii) pre-computed Monte Carlo results (4,000 draws, κ=200 primary; κ=50 robustness check); (iv) bootstrap contrast files; (v) Python scripts to reproduce all experiments, bootstrap analyses, LaTeX macros, and manuscript figures; (vi) LaTeX manuscript source.

Key finding: Normalisation is the dominant driver of Pareto attainment. Switching from min-max to vector normalisation shifts greedy attainment by +25.4 pp (κ=200); the SAW–TOPSIS contrast is equivalent to zero at κ=200 but rises to +20.4 pp at κ=50.

Changelog v1.2 (2026-10-29): Repository renamed to mcdm-landfill-pareto-paper; Zenodo GitHub integration enabled. Title aligned with submitted manuscript. Aspect convention corrected throughout (geographic azimuth; paper/scripts/utils/aspect_utils.py). κ-sensitivity qualified in abstract, highlights, and main text; bootstrap contrasts for both κ values in paper/results/bootstrap_k50_k200.csv. PRESPEC documents under paper/docs/prespec/; Zenodo archive date serves as external timestamp for PRESPEC_SANTIAGO.

The provenance script paper/scripts/analysis/verify_macros_permanent.py recomputes all primary quantitative claims.
